Observed:
- Asymptomatic swelling in the right lower half of the face
- Reduced mouth opening
- Gross right facial asymmetry
- Ovoid subcutaneous swelling with ill-defined borders
- Elevated and glistening right buccal mucosa
- 62-year-old man
- Two-week history of facial swelling
- Two prior similar episodes over eight years
- No pain or fever
- Known diabetic on regular medication
- 6 × 6 cm ovoid subcutaneous swelling
- Swelling extended from the level of the right lateral canthus to 1 cm below the corner of the mouth
- Restricted mouth opening due to the mass
- Contrast-enhanced CT showed a well-defined soft-tissue mass with cystic areas
- Intracystic loculations with dense cystic content
- Erosion of the posterior buccal cortex without perforation of the maxilla
- Maxillary antrum was compressed
Differential diagnosis:
1. Buccal space abscess
2. Dentigerous cyst
3. Staphylococcal lymphadenitis
4. Sialadenitis
5. Kimura disease
